title: AI-assisted browser game development: one danger rule, three UI surfaces, and a local review fixture
author: FloriMTV
selftext:
I’m developing World of Frontiers, a browser space MMO inspired by DarkOrbit. I use AI assistance for code work and some assets. Here is a concrete example of the implementation and review process, using a small change to the danger warnings.



The design constraint is simple: Dead Sector opens at level 18, but unlocking access does not mean your current ship is ready. The warning recommends a Leviathan or a group; PvP is enabled there too.



In the implementation, the sector’s danger flag lives in the shared map catalogue. A small shared helper turns that flag into the warning label, advice and markup. The star chart, entrance gate and persistent HUD warning all read from that shared logic. That keeps the AI-assisted code work tied to the same explicit rule across the three views.



For visual review, the project has a local-only fixture that imports the actual chart, gate and HUD components. It supplies a synthetic player state so the warning screens can be inspected directly. The fixture offers different scenes, viewport sizes and languages. The stills in this clip were captured from its English desktop views.



This is the distinction I find useful in an AI-assisted workflow: source inspection can establish which condition triggers the warning, and a rendered capture can show whether the text is readable. Neither proves that players notice it at the right time or that the combat is balanced. Those remain playtest questions.



How do you check AI-assisted UI changes that appear in several places? Do you use small fixtures like this, full gameplay captures, or both—and what kinds of errors does each approach miss?



Clip: 6 seconds of earlier staged combat, followed by new local captures of the warning UI, explicitly labelled as still images. This demonstrates the interface, not the latest Dead Sector combat balance. Music: our original “Sternenordnung”. AI assists development and some assets.
